First elected in 2006, Austin Mayor Pro Tem and Council Member Sheryl Cole has the honor of being Austin's first African American woman to be elected to its City Council.
A graduate from the University of Texas' accounting and law programs, Cole worked for two years as a certified public accountant at Big Five accounting firm Ernst & Young, and then was staff counsel at the Texas Municipal League before she was elected to the Austin City Council in 2006.
Since then, Cole has been re-elected twice -- first in 2009 and again in 2012 -- and assumed the role of mayor pro tem in 2011. 
An Austin resident of more than 30 years, Cole is a strong advocate for affordable housing and improving Austin transportation. She is known for handling politically charged issues with care, striving to reach compromise and consensus among parties. 
Over the years, she has been involved with numerous intergovernmental committees including the Capital Area Metropolitan Planning Organization Transportation Policy Board, Downtown Alliance Austin and ABIA Development Corp.
For her leadership, she's received the Distinguished Achievement in Public Service award from the National Black Public Administrators and the Texas Homeless Network's Outstanding Community Service award, among others. 
In addition to her role as mother of three boys, Cole is past president of the Lee Elementary School PTA and a former board member of Leadership Austin, the Austin Area Urban League and Communities in Schools. She said she welcomes opportunities to mentor aspiring leaders.
